questions.q: Volume of $3MNaOH$ (formula weight $40g{mol}^{- 1}$ ) which can be prepared from $84g$ of $NaOH$ is ____\times {10}^{- 1}{dm}^{3}.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Number of moles = Mass / Molar mass

Molar mass of NaOH=$40$ g/mol

By Using the definition of molarity to find the volume of the solution:

Molarity= $\dfrac{Number of moles of solute}{Volume of solution (in liters)}$

$M = \dfrac{nNaOH}{{V}_{sol} ( \text{in}L )} ⇒ 3 = \dfrac{( 84 / 40 )}{V} ⇒ V = 0 . 7L = 7 \times {10}^{- 1}L$

questions.q: The molarity of ${HNO}_{3}$ in a sample which has density $1.4g / mL$ and mass percentage of $63%$ is ________ (Molecular Weight of ${HNO}_{3} = 63$ )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$63%\dfrac{w}{w} ⟶ HN{O}_{3}$ solution
$M = \dfrac{63 \times 1.4}{63 \times 100} \times 1000mole / L$
$M = 14mole / L$

questions.q: $1g$ of a carbonate  \left({M}_{2}{CO}_{3}\right)$ on treatment with excess $HCl$ produces $0 . 01mol$ of ${CO}_{2}$. The molar mass of ${M}_{2}{CO}_{3}$~is ${gmol}^{- 1}$. (Nearest integer)$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
From Balanced chemical reaction,

${M}_{2}{CO}_{3} + 2HCl \to 2MCl + {H}_{2}O + {CO}_{2}$

Here from this, we~get:

$0 . 01mol{CO}_{2} ≡ 0 . 01mol{M}_{2}{CO}_{3} ≡ 1g{M}_{2}{CO}_{3}$

~We know that,

Number of moles =~$\dfrac{Givenmass}{Molarmass}$

$⇒$Molar mass of~${M}_{2}{CO}_{3} = \dfrac{Givenmassof{M}_{2}{CO}_{3}}{NumberofMolesof{M}_{2}{CO}_{3}} = \dfrac{1}{0 . 01} = 100g / mol$

questions.q: The number of $N$ atoms in $681g$ of ${C}_{7}{H}_{5}{N}_{3}{O}_{6}$ is $x \times {10}^{21}$. The value of $x$~is  \left({N}_{A} = 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23}{mol}^{- 1}\right)$ (Nearest Integer)$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given mass of compounds $= 681g$

Molar mass of ${C}_{7}{H}_{5}{N}_{3}{O}_{6} = 12 \times 7 + 5 \times 1 + 14 \times 3 + 6 \times 16$

$= 84 + 5 + 42 + 96$

$= 227$

Number of moles of compound $= \dfrac{681}{227} = 3$ moles

Number of moles of $N = 3 \times$number of moles of compound

$= 3 \times 3 = 9$ moles

Number of atoms of N~$= 9 \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23}$

$= 5418 \times {10}^{21}$

So $x = 5418$

questions.q: An organic compound gives $0 . 220g$ of ${CO}_{2}$~and $0 . 126g$ of ${H}_{2}O$ on complete combustion. If the $%$ of carbon is $24$ then the $%$ of hydrogen is _________ \times {10}^{– 1} . (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Moles of& ${CO}_{2} = \dfrac{0 . 22}{44} = \dfrac{1}{200}$

Then,

Mass of~$C = \dfrac{0 . 220}{44} \times 12 = 0 . 06g$

$% ofC = \dfrac{0 . 06}{W} \times 100 = 24$

(W= Wt.of organic compound)

$W = 0 . 25$

Moles of~${H}_{2}O = \dfrac{0 . 126}{18} = 0 . 007$

Moles of~$H = 0 . 007 \times 2 = 0 . 014g$

$% ofHydrogen = \dfrac{0 . 014 \times 1}{W} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 014 \times 1}{0 . 25} \times 100 = 5 . 6$

$= 56 \times {10}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
The mole fraction of a solute in a $100$ molal~aqueous solution ________~$\times {10}^{- 2} .$

(Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Given : Atomic masses:~$H: 1 . 0u, O: 16 . 0u$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$100$ molal aqueous solution means there is $100$ mole solute in $1kg = 1000gm$ water.

Now,

mole-fraction of solute$= \dfrac{n\text{solute}}{{n}_{solute } + {n}_{solvent }}$

$= \dfrac{100}{100 + \dfrac{1000}{18}} = \dfrac{1800}{2800} = 0 . 6428$

$= 64 . 28 \times {10}^{- 2}$

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction:

$3{PbCl}_{2} + 2\left({NH}_{4}\right)3{PO}_{4} \to {Pb}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2 + 6{NH}_{4}Cl$

If $72mmol{PbCl}_{2}$ is mixed with $50mmol$ of \left({NH}_{4}\right)3{PO}_{4},$ then amount of ${Pb}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2$ formed in $mmol$. (nearest integer)

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The reaction is given as,

$3{PbCl}_{2} + 2\left({NH}_{4}\right)3{PO}_{4} \to {Pb}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2 + 6{NH}_{4}Cl$

The products formed in the above reaction is ${Pb}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2\text{and}{NH}_{4}Cl$ .

According to the above stoichiometric equation, three mole of each lead chloride and two moles of \left({NH}_{4}\right)3{PO}_{4}$ is required to make one mole of ${Pb}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2\text{and}6\text{moles of}{NH}_{4}Cl$

Here the Limiting Reagent is ${PbCl}_{2}$

$mmol$ of ${Pb}_{3} ( {PO}_{4}{)}_{2}$ formed

$= \dfrac{mmol\text{of}{PbCl}_{2}\text{reacted}}{3} = \dfrac{72}{3}$

$= 24m mol$

$

questions.q: Mass of methane required to produce $22g$ of $CO$ after complete combustion is g. (Given Molar mass in g mol-1, $C = 12 . 0$, $H = 1 . 0$, $O = 16 . 0 )$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The molecular mass of methane is $16g / mol$.

The reaction is as follows,

${CH}_{4} + 2{O}_{2} \to {CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Moles of ${CO}_{2} = \dfrac{mass}{molar mass} = \dfrac{22}{44} = 0 . 5$

So, required moles of ${CH}_{4} = 0 . 5$

${Mass of CH}_{4} = 0 . 5 \times 16 = 8gm$

questions.q: Chlorophyll extracted from the crushed green leaves was dissolved in water to make $2L$ solution of $Mg$ of concentration $48 \mathrm{ppm}$. The number of atoms of $Mg$ in this solution is $x \times {10}^{20}$ atoms. The value of $x$~is (Nearest Integer) (Given : Atomic mass of $Mg$ is $24g{mol}^{- 1}$, ${N}_{A} = 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23}{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria that is essential for photosynthesis. Its central structure is an aromatic porphyrin ring system with a sequestered magnesium atom.

$ppm = \dfrac{W{M}_{g}}{Vsol} \times {10}^{6} = 48$

$⇒ {W}_{Mg} = \dfrac{48 \times 2 \times 1000}{106}$

$= 48 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3}g$

${n}_{Mg} = \dfrac{WMg}{24} = \dfrac{48 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{24}$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 3}$

Number of $Mg$ atoms~$= 4 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23} = 4 \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{20}$

$= 4 \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{20}$

$= 24 . 08 \times {10}^{20}$

$∴ x = 24 . 08$

questions.q: A $1 . 84mg$ sample of polyhydric alcoholic compound '$X$' of molar mass $92 . 0g / mol$ gave $1 . 344mL$ of ${H}_{2}$ gas at STP. The number of alcoholic hydrogen present in compound '$X$' is
questions.subject: Chemistry

Number of moles of alcoholic compound& $= \dfrac{Givenmass}{Molarmass} = \dfrac{1 . 84 \times {10}^{- 3}}{92 . 0} = 2 \times {10}^{- 5}moles$

Number of moles of hydrogen gas produced~$= \dfrac{VolumeofgasatSTP}{22400ml} = \dfrac{1 . 344}{22400} = 6 \times {10}^{- 5}moles$

Monohydric~alcohol will react with active metal to give~$\dfrac{1}{2}mole$& of hydrogen gas.

Since per mole of given alcohol is giving 3 moles of hydrogen gas.

So number of alcoholic hydrogen present in compound should be =6.

questions.q:
The molarity of $1L$ orthophosphoric acid \left({H}_{3}{PO}_{4}\right)$ having $70 %$ purity by weight (specific gravity $1 .54 g{cm}^{- 3}$) is ______ $M$. (Molar mass of ${H}_{3}{PO}_{4} = 98g{mol}^{- 1}$)

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Specific gravity (density) $= 1 .54 g / cc$.

Volume $= 1L = 1000ml$

Mass of solution $= 1 .54 \times 1000$

$= 1540g$

$%$ purity of ${H}_{3}{PO}_{4}$ is $70 %$

So weight of ${H}_{3}{PO}_{4} = 0 .7 \times 1540 = 1078g$

Mole of ${H}_{3}{PO}_{4} = \dfrac{mass}{molarmass} = \dfrac{1078}{98} = 11$

Molarity= $\dfrac{No . ofmolesofsolute}{VolumeofsolutioninL}$

Molarity $= \dfrac{11}{1L} = 11M$

questions.q: $0 . 5g$ of an organic compound (X) with $60 %$ carbon will produce $\times {10}^{- 1}g$ of ${CO}_{2}$& on complete combustion.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$

To calculate the mass percent of an element in a compound, we divide the mass of the element in 1 mole of the compound by the compound's molar mass and multiply the result by 100.

The combustion reaction is& $C \left(s\right) + {O}_{2} \left($g\right)\overset{}{→}{CO}_{2}\left($g\right)$

$C % = $\dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{\text{Wt. of}{CO}_{2}}{ Wt. of organic compound } \times$100$

$60 = $\dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{\text{Wt. of}{CO}_{2}}{0 . 5} \times$100$

Wt. of~${CO}_{2} = 1 . 1$

$

questions.q: The formula of a gaseous hydrocarbon which requires 6 times of its own volume of ${O}_{2}$ for complete oxidation and produces $4$ times its own volume of ${CO}_{2}$ is ${C}_{x}{H}_{y} .$ The value of $y$ is ________.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Combustion reaction.

${C}_{x}{H}_{y ( g )} + \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right){O}_{2} \left(g\right) \to {xCO}_{2} \left($g\right) + $\ddfrac{y}{2}{H}_{2}O\left(ℓ\right)$

$\begin{cases}V \text{ and } 6V \text{ and } - \\ - \text{ and } - \text{ and } Vx = 4V\end{cases}$

$⇒ x = 4$

Since:~\left(I\right){Vo}_{2} = 6 \times {V}_{{C}_{x}{H}_{y}}$

$⇒ V\left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right) =6V$

$⇒ \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right) =6 ⇒ 4 + \dfrac{y}{4} =6$

$⇒ y = 8$

$

questions.q:
The density of $3M$~solution of $NaCl$ is $1 . 0g{mL}^{- 1}$. Molality of the solution is ______ \times {10}^{- 2}m$ (Nearest integer).

Given: Molar mass of $Na$ and $Cl$ is $23$ and $35 . 5g{mol}^{- 1} respectively.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Formula unit mass of sodium chloride =& $23 + 35 . 5{gmol}^{- 1} = 58 . 5{gmol}^{- 1}$
$∴ m ( molality ) = \dfrac{1000 \times M}{1000 \times d - M \times M . W\text{of solute}}$~ ~...$( M = Molarityofsolution )$

$= \dfrac{1000 \times 3}{1000 \times 1 - ( 3 \times 58 . 5 )} = 3 . 64$

$= 364 \times {10}^{- 2}$
